_provenance: Recorded 2026-10-17 on a throwaway claimed Plex Media Server 1.42.2.10156-f737b826c (Docker on the test host, owner account with Plex Pass INACTIVE, so downloads need no Pass) through Plex for Android 2026.19.1's download flow: createDownloadQueue -> addItemToDownloadQueue (keys + decision params) -> fetchDownloadQueueItems polled every 3 s -> fetchDecision -> getMediaPath (HEAD, a 1 KiB Range, the whole file) -> removeDownloadQueueItems, with the app's X-Plex-* headers and the token in the query. Library: 30 s 1280x720 h264/aac mkv clips (a movie, two episodes). `original` adds with no quality params; `capped` with maxVideoBitrate=720&videoResolution=640x360. The second run adds directPlay=1&directStream=1 and an X-Plex-Client-Profile-Extra allowing mkv in the query, which changed nothing: every item is converted to one mp4 (the profile's static target), one at a time. Token, Date and Last-Modified removed; media bodies by length only.

Now, this means war. But who will win?
